dimension_grades.evidence: Project Alpha and Blockers & Risks sections are written as narrative paragraphs, not bullet points.
The Blockers & Risks section contains multi-sentence prose paragraphs rather than self-contained 1–2 line bullets.
'Resolve the database migration issue' and 'Figure out coverage for Jake's absence' appear in both Blockers & Risks and Next Steps sections.

Next Steps contains 7 bullets including items like 'Update the project tracker' and 'Schedule sync with Platform team' that could be folded into project-level sections or omitted from a leadership update.
The email opens with 'Hope you had a good weekend! I wanted to give you a rundown...' — pleasantries and context-setting, not a status summary.
There is no single summary sentence capturing wins and timeline shifts; the draft buries both across separate sections.
No line in the opening (or anywhere) explicitly signals whether the reader needs to act or not.
There is no summary line at all, so no label (plain or otherwise) is present.
The draft uses alarm language: 'pretty significant setback,' 'real problem,' and 'scrambling to figure out a workaround.'
'could potentially push things back' is vague with no concrete estimate such as '~1 week.'
'Will keep you posted as we learn more' gives no specific date by which the resolution path will be clear.
The draft never states that the database issue or staffing gap does not need director escalation; it leaves the reader to infer.
The draft contains no internet-style abbreviations or casual shorthand labels (e.g., no 'TL;DR', 'FYI', 'ASAP').
The closing uses 'Best regards' which is overly formal, and the opening filler ('Hope you had a good weekend') adds unnecessary padding rather than approachable directness.
The verbose narrative paragraphs and weekend pleasantry show no awareness that Maria reads on mobile between meetings and prefers concise, bottom-line communication.
